key_insight: No reconstruction method wins across all flows: classical estimators remain competitive, while learned methods gain advantages with fewer sensors or poorly observed fields.
engineering_relevance: Sparse-sensor flow reconstruction should balance accuracy, uncertainty calibration and computational cost rather than defaulting to learned models.
method: Benchmark 10 learned and 5 classical methods across cylinder wakes, 2D Kolmogorov turbulence and large-scale 3D isotropic turbulence.
Use leakage-controlled splits and shared sensor draws for comparable evaluations.
Measure per-channel error, ensemble spread, calibration, spectra and computational cost.
evidence_signal: Classical methods lead on cylinder wakes, inverse-distance weighting matches top learned methods on observed 3D channels, and Kolmogorov rankings differ between pointwise error and probabilistic scoring.
watch_item: Generative ensembles remain underdispersed, and improving ensemble quality through larger sampling budgets increases computational cost.
paper_title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
